blocks.text: INQUIRER.net / Updated as of: 07:36 AM November 09, 2026

MANILA, Philippines —The Senate impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte resumes on Monday, Nov. 9, marking Day 40 of the proceedings, after a nearly monthlong recess. Her defense team is set to present witnesses and evidence to counter allegations of unexplained wealth and undeclared assets, amid calls from the prosecution and the public for Duterte to personally take the witness stand and answer the accusations.

items: Suzette Balucanag-Punay, corporate counsel of GenCorp Industries Inc. and Metro City Chow Foods Corp., was initially scheduled to testify Monday but will likely appear on Wednesday due to a scheduled MRI scan.
Senate impeachment court spokesperson Reginald Tongol said 22 of the 24 subpoenas requested by the defense have been served.
Punay is expected to testify on the general information sheets and audited financial statements of the two corporations from 2022 to 2025.
Chief prosecutor Gerville Luistro urged the Vice President to take the witness stand, saying she is the only person who can directly explain the allegations against her.

Prosecutors cited the findings of forensic financial analyst Alexander Cabrera, who estimated that Duterte may have at least P817.87 million in unexplained assets, with broader projections reaching more than P1.5 billion.

The prosecution presented land titles for two properties registered under the name of Duterte’s husband, lawyer Manases Carpio, which were allegedly not reflected in her statements of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALNs)./dp
